## In-seat review of record — `domain:ui` @ objectui seat

**Verdict: land.** Clause-② was declared **no** at dispatch (objectui#8854 comment 5624276737) and that holds: nothing published moved, no schema or validation path changed, and the condition I named as the one thing that would flip it — needing a declared-schema change to make the block validate — did not arise.

### ⭐ You falsified my ZONE 3, and it was the load-bearing part of the brief

I suggested running the block through `flowNodeObject()` / `FlowEdgeSchema`. You measured the door instead: `clientValidation.ts`'s `LOADERS.flow` resolves the spec's `FlowSchema`, and `ResourceEditPage` calls `validateMetadataDraft(type, draft)` with the editor's **entire body**.

⇒ My suggested route would have graded the fence per node and per edge, reported **green**, and shipped a block that still cannot be saved. That is not a near miss — it is precisely how the third defect survived objectui#8483 *and* objectui#8854, two cards filed against this same fence. A per-part check answers a question no reader asks; what a reader does is paste the whole thing.

This is the fourth time this session a dev has caught a seat error, and it is the one with the largest blast radius: the acceptance oracle I specified could not have detected the defect that mattered most.

### The third defect, and the in-place fix — endorsed

`FlowSchema` requires `name`, `label` and `type`; the fence carried none of the three while being captioned *"a `flow` draft"*. Repairing only the two ruled defects would have left a pasted copy refused three more times, and a third card against this fence would have followed.

⛔ My ZONE 1.3 fenced "do not check the other blocks while you're there" — and you did not. This is the **same block**, the same defect, the same reader-pastes-it-and-is-refused failure. Fixing it in place was right, and your reason is the decisive one: **filing it instead would have shipped a PR whose own claim — "the documented draft now saves" — was false**, with an acceptance test that could not pass. Naming it loudly in the body and changeset so it can be stripped independently is the correct way to take that latitude.

The form is right too: `{ name, label, type: 'autolaunched' }` matches what this repo's own `buildFlowSkeleton` emits, so the example teaches the producer's shape rather than a shape invented for the docs.

### On the test's design

Two choices carry it, and both are the right ones:

- **The fence is EXTRACTED, never retyped.** A hand copy drifts from the file it claims to pin and therefore pins nothing — reproducing a snippet inside the test would have re-created the exact defect the card is about. And the extractor **throws** on a moved heading, a removed fence or a non-JSON body rather than passing vacuously on an empty fixture.
- **`stripLineComments` is string-aware.** A blunt `replace(/\/\/.*$/gm, '')` would cut inside `"${days <= 30}"`. Six lines to avoid silently truncating a value is the right trade.

And the green carries its controls: three mutations re-injecting each repaired defect, each required to be refused **by name and at the right path**. A `safeParse` that succeeds proves nothing if the schema accepts everything; that pairing is what makes it a measurement.

### The ZONE 2 falsifications, all of which improved on my framing

- **Changeset (2c).** My note guessed the README might owe one because `app-shell` is published. Wrong mechanism: you ran the gate twice and found it **subtracts `*.md` outside `src/`**, so the README owes nothing on its own — the new **test file under `src/`** is what flips it, because the gate has no test carve-out. A changeset is owed, by the test, not the docs. `patch` with in-repo precedent cited is the right call.
- **Edge ids (2d).** Free-form: `z.string()` with `checks=[]`, and nothing reads a convention back — which is why two in-repo producers disagree (`buildFlowSkeleton` writes `e1`, `FlowCanvas` mints `edge_1`). Matching the documented skeleton is the right tiebreak among equals.
- **`position` requires both coordinates**, and the README already said so — so it was correct as written and stayed unchanged. Likewise the Layout bullet's `ui`-is-refused-with-a-422 sentence: it was never wrong, it was **contradicted by the block above it**, and it now agrees. Auditing it clause by clause and reporting "unchanged" is a better answer than editing it to look busy.

### I verified the one NEW factual claim you added to the README

The Edges bullet now asserts that a bare `condition` string is widened to the ADR-0089 envelope. Checked against the installed `@objectstack/spec@17.4.0`, controls lit: the transform is `z.string().min(1).transform((source) => ({ dialect: 'cel', source }))`, and the refusal text names **`edge.condition`** explicitly as a structural condition alongside a node's `config.condition`. ⇒ **The claim is true.** Worth verifying rather than taking on trust, because a new prose assertion in a README is the same defect class this card exists to close, pointed forward.

### ⚠️ One observation, explicitly UNMEASURED and deliberately not filed

`FlowSchema` accepts the condition because the widening only requires a non-blank string — it does not judge whether the source is valid CEL. The fence's `"${days <= 30}"` is template-style interpolation, not the bare CEL the spec's own prescription illustrates (`record.rating >= 4`). So the draft can parse and still carry a condition the evaluator may not honour.

⛔ I have **not** measured whether `${…}` is honoured on this path, that syntax predates this card, and my own ZONE 1.3 fenced widening. Recording it only so the next reader of this fence has the question in front of them; ⛔ not filed, and ⛔ not a reason to hold this PR.

### Gates

Landing on every-check-green. Your handling of `check:doc-snippets` / `check:doc-examples` / `check:readme-exports` — diagnosing exit 2 as PREREQUISITE NOT MET on an unbuilt tree and then driving each to 0 after building, rather than reporting them as red or as NOT MEASURED — is exactly the standard, and it leaves nothing undeclared.
